summary: The recorded main base still reproduced the parser defects. Existing upstream PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35625 contains a complete candidate correction; it was applied cleanly to this base and independently verified. With response-position tool indexes compared consistently, cohere_command4 and gemma4 expose an index-semantics defect rather than a streaming-only mismatch. The candidate also fixes GLM numeric typing, Minimax empty calls/start-marker buffering, Mistral repeated calls, and Step3 empty/multiple-call parsing.

tests.what_was_measured: Before the correction at the recorded base: corrected issue fixture reproduced GLM/GLM45/GLM47 numeric type divergence, the missing Minimax call, and Step3 one-shot/streaming divergence. Raw output: reports/j-570829e32467/before.txt
After the correction: all eight issue cases agree, with response-position indexes 0/1 retained for repeated calls. Raw output: reports/j-570829e32467/after.txt

Eight targeted regression tests passed, including whole-input, character-at-a-time, and every two-chunk split boundary: 8 passed and 876 subtests passed. Raw output: reports/j-570829e32467/pytest-streaming-parity.txt
The complete registered function-call unit directory passed: 548 tests and 897 subtests. Raw output: reports/j-570829e32467/pytest-function-call.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect is deterministic parser logic operating on supplied strings and tool schemas; it does not execute model or GPU kernels. No GPU claim is made.

remaining_limitations: No model-serving or model-architecture behavior was tested; this validates only parser output for deterministic supplied text.
The candidate's partial Minimax start-marker holdback is defensive for character splits inside a marker; the issue states real tokenization emits that marker atomically.

The pre-fix corrected reproducer stores calls by tool_index, so the base's duplicate-index defect collapses the two Mistral entries in that diagnostic. The regression suite independently checks response-position indexes and all split points after correction.
